THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE 93

Some of the original poems found in the papers are of considerable interest and merit. An article from "Texas University" (publication not cited) entitled "Inspiration" was published in the January 1, 1885 issue. The following editorial in November, 1886, taken from the State School Journal is "Into Each Life Some Rain Must Fall." The articles were often in "flowery" language, which provided opportunity for brilliant displays of imagery; but quite frequently this was the spirit of the times. About the time he reached the College, a student had had it all a decided lack of awareness, stand out more boldly in the memory. The two which follow are remembered by Mr. Sam W. McKee and related by him:

"Data to the Wall, J. Reeben"—About the year of 1884, in order to meet the needs of the fast-growing institution the College building had been greatly enlarged; and when it was quite a new and commodious structure (it was later called the East addition, and when completed it was quite a valuable building of which we were all justly proud). The lower part was used for recitations, with the story arranged and fitted to accommodate the Business and Commercial department; and the basement was to be occupied by the intermediate department with Prof. F. Montgomery as its teacher.

The lower story was fitted up with good taste, with the inside wall being shiplapped with white pine lumber. Among the full quota of students in the department were tables arranged in rows with aisles running between each row.
